title: Regulated – consent required, transcript not retained
description: For meetings where consent has to come first and as little meeting content as possible is kept. Nothing is recorded or kept until consent is given: Meeting Consent mode Opt-in with the each-participant rule, a meeting may only use this mode or a stricter one, streaming clients without a consent step are refused, the Virtual Participant leaves after an objection, and evidence screenshots are kept. Stream Audio/Video and the Desktop Capture App cannot collect each participant's consent, so Start is refused from them under this preset; use a Virtual Participant on a join that supports each-participant consent. A Virtual Participant on the Webex join cannot tell who is present, so it never meets the each-participant rule, and a meeting cannot switch to the less strict owner-attests rule, so such a meeting is not transcribed; on the Teams browser join the chat senders and the participant list are read from the Teams page, which has not yet been confirmed with a Virtual Participant in a live meeting. While consent is awaited, a Virtual Participant listens for consent and objections said aloud and addressed to LMA: the meeting audio is processed by the meeting's transcription engine, and only the reply events are kept on the consent record. Turn Meeting Consent › Read spoken replies off, which this preset leaves as it is, to read replies in the chat only and send no meeting audio anywhere before consent. See "What each platform supports" in docs/meeting-consent.md. The transcript is deleted 15 minutes after the summary is written, and any recording that is still stored (an uploaded meeting's audio, for example) as soon as the summary is written; meeting audio, screen video from streaming clients and Virtual Participant meeting video are not recorded, personal information is redacted from transcripts (in en-US, en-AU, en-GB and es-US), the meeting chat is not added to the transcript, and Amazon Bedrock models run within this deployment's geography. The meeting assistant and summary settings it sets keep their shipped defaults: anyone in the meeting may make a request, answered from the current meeting only with no access to the meeting context and checklist; web search and the installed MCP servers are available; and new meetings start with no summary profile. Meetings are shared with the people on their participant list (Meeting Sharing on), who see a read-only page without the owner's own material. Every other setting stays as it is. Some controls are stack parameters rather than settings, so they are not part of any profile and have to be set when the stack is deployed or updated: LogLevel (INFO or WARN; DEBUG logs meeting content), the retention periods MeetingRecordExpirationInDays, TranscriptionExpirationInDays, AudioRecordingExpirationInDays and CloudWatchLogsExpirationInDays, and EnableVideoRecording (meeting video from the Virtual Participant, the Desktop Capture App, the Stream Audio/Video page and the browser extension). See "Where meeting content is processed" in docs/infrastructure-and-security.md.

values.videoNoticeText: Video of the meeting, including shared screens and any visible camera feeds, is also recorded.
